topic: Korean public restrooms are free by default. Public Toilets Act (공중화장실 등에 관한 법률, enacted 2004-01-29, in force 2004-07-30): paid toilets are the exception and must be reported to the local office and signposted (Art. 11); public institutions must open their restrooms to the public unless security forbids it, and local offices can designate private buildings as 'open restrooms' with a sign (Art. 9). Covers subway and rail stations, bus terminals, parks, highway rest stops, gas stations (Art. 3). Women's stalls must be at least men's toilets plus urinals combined; 1.5x at venues of 1,000+ and busy highway rest stops (Art. 7(1),(2); Decree Art. 6). Emergency bells required where local ordinance lists (Art. 7(4), added 2021-07-20, in force 2023-07-21). Child toilets, sinks and diaper tables in men's and women's rooms (Art. 7-2). Decree Art. 7: caretaker with posted contact, disinfection 3x/week Apr-Sep and 1x/week Oct-Mar, no trash bin inside stalls (from 2018-01-01), sanitary bin in women's stalls. Background: 1999 Suwon mayor Sim Jae-deok founded a toilet association ahead of the 2002 World Cup.
title: In Korea, Public Toilets Are Free

slides.kicker: NO COINS. NO CODE. NO RECEIPT.
slides.headline: In Korea, public toilets are **free.**
slides.note: And most of them have toilet paper.

slides.headline: Free is **the default**
slides.body: Under Korean law, a toilet you pay for is the exception. The owner has to report it to the local office and put up a sign. Subway stations, parks, bus terminals and highway rest stops charge nothing.

slides.headline: Public buildings **must share**
slides.body: Government offices have to open their restrooms to anyone walking by, unless security says no. Cities can also sign up private buildings as "open restrooms" and mark them with a sign at the door.

slides.headline: It started with **a World Cup**
slides.body: In 1999, ahead of the 2002 World Cup, Suwon's mayor started a toilet association to fix the country's restrooms. He became known as "Mr. Toilet." A national law followed in 2004.

slides.headline: No bin **next to the toilet**
slides.body: Since 2018, public restroom stalls are not allowed to have a trash bin for used paper. You flush it. Women's stalls get a small bin for sanitary products instead.

slides.headline: the stalls for **women**
slides.body: At big stadiums, concert halls and busy highway rest stops, women's stalls must be at least 1.5 times the men's toilets and urinals combined. Everywhere else, at least equal.

slides.headline: A button **for help**
slides.body: Restrooms on the local safety list must have an emergency bell. One press connects to the building manager or the police. The rule has been in force since 2023.

slides.headline: Built for **kids, too**
slides.body: Public restrooms need child-size toilets and sinks. Baby changing tables go in the men's room as well as the women's, so either parent can do it.

slides.headline: Clean, **by rule**
slides.body: Every public restroom needs a caretaker, with a phone number posted at the entrance. It must be disinfected three times a week in summer and once a week in winter.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.

caption:
In Korea, you don't pay to use a public toilet. Subway stations, parks, rest stops: free, and usually with paper.

By law, a paid toilet is the exception, and government buildings have to open their restrooms to anyone.

Do you pay for public toilets where you live?
reply: Travel tip: if you need a restroom fast in Korea, look for a subway station, a highway rest stop or a gas station. Gas stations are covered by the same public toilet law. And don't look for a bin in the stall: toilet paper goes in the bowl.
fact_check: 1장: 공중화장실 무료가 기본 — 공중화장실법 제2조5호·제11조(유료화장실은 신고·표지 필요한 예외). '대부분 휴지 있음'은 일반 관행 수준 표현.
2장: 제11조 ① 유료화장실 신고, ④ 표지 부착. 제3조 적용 범위: 도시철도 역사·철도역·여객터미널·도시공원·도로 휴게시설 등 (법제처 현행, 2023-07-21 시행본).
3장: 제9조 ① 공공기관 화장실 공중 개방 의무(보안·안전 예외), ②·③ 민간 시설 개방화장실 지정·표지.
4장: 1999년 심재덕 당시 수원시장, 2002 월드컵 앞두고 화장실협회 창설(주간경향). 'Mr. Toilet' 별명은 국내외 보도 통칭. 법 제정 2004-01-29 법률 제7129호, 시행 2004-07-30(국가법령정보센터 연혁). 슬라이드는 '법이 뒤따랐다'로 인과 단정 안 함.
5장: 시행령 제7조3호 대변기 칸막이 안 휴지통 금지, 4호 여성용 칸 위생용품 수거함. 2018-01-01 시행(정책브리핑 korea.kr 148846934).
6장: 법 제7조① 여성 대변기 ≥ 남성 대·소변기 합, ② 1.5배 이상 — 시행령 제6조: 수용 1천명 이상 공연장·관람장·전시장·야외음악당·유원지, 일 편도 5만대 이상 고속도로 휴게소.
7장: 법 제7조④ 비상벨(관리자 또는 경찰관서 연결) 등 안전관리시설, 대상은 조례로 지정. 2021-07-20 신설, 2023-07-21 시행(행안부 안전한 사용환경 페이지).
8장: 법 제7조의2 ① 어린이용 대·소변기·세면대, ② 남성 및 여성 화장실에 영유아 기저귀교환대(대통령령 기준 시설).
9장: 시행령 제7조1호 관리인·연락처 게시, 2호 소독 4~9월 주 3회 이상, 10~3월 주 1회 이상.
reply: 제3조11호 석유판매업(주유소) 시설도 적용 대상. 휴지는 변기에 — 시행령 제7조3호.
